source.title: Theory of Deep Learning III: explaining the non-overfitting puzzle
source.authors: T. Poggio; Kenji Kawaguchi; Q. Liao; B. Miranda; L. Rosasco; X. Boix; J. Hidary; H. Mhaskar

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains the same CIFAR-10 convolutional architecture on natural and randomly scrambled labels and reports training and test classification behavior, directly reproducing the random-label memorization and natural-label generalization comparison.
record.gate_note: Figures 1 and 6 also report results across training-set sizes or model sizes. Figure 5 reports cross-entropy loss over model size; these are recorded as separate measures. The text gives qualitative descriptions rather than exact plotted values. Batch size is fixed at 100 in Figure 5 and is not a tested comparison.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 directly repeats the natural-label versus scrambled-label training/test classification comparison underlying V1. The width sweep also bears on V2 in a different architecture, although its fixed 70-epoch budget does not establish training to convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose that local equivalence between deep-network and linear gradient dynamics explains loss overfitting alongside classification robustness on suitable datasets through implicit regularization and margin maximization. Their argument depends on assumptions about minima and data; they explicitly leave quantitative performance bounds and why networks perform as well as they do unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Direct random-label memorization and natural-label generalization comparison on a smaller 5-layer all-convolutional CIFAR network; no data augmentation or regularization.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior differs between cross-entropy loss and classification error as model size increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Test cross-entropy increases with model size while classification error remains unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing convolutional-network size can worsen held-out cross-entropy without worsening classification error.

fits_no_version.finding: Repeated weight perturbations followed by retraining increase weight norms and test loss while training error returns to zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbation and retraining can worsen held-out loss without preventing exact training classification.

record.problems: The paper focuses on gradient descent for its analysis, while some experiments use SGD. Numerical outcomes in the relevant figures are described qualitatively in the supplied text, without exact values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: The original architectures and ImageNet setting are not examined. Chance-level random-label held-out accuracy cannot be verified from the supplied figure text.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 trained to convergence, and a precisely identified width at which training error first reaches zero.
No trained convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison.
No comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps across similarly fitted networks or against competing measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

missing.what: Natural-label and scrambled-label training/test classification results for polynomial-activation convolutional networks, recorded as separate condition rows.
Polynomial convolutional-network width sweep, including zero training error in the overparameterized regime and the reported lack of classification overfitting.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Remove the record's V1 limits_scope label based on cross-entropy: V1 concerns held-out accuracy, so loss overfitting does not qualify that claim. Figure captions and prose are available, but the supplied text does not expose the plotted curves well enough to recover numerical values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test small Inception, AlexNet, or MLPs, or Inception V3 on ImageNet; tests a 5-layer all-convolutional CIFAR network.
The paper varies model size in an all-convolutional CIFAR network, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to convergence on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.
Does not compare convolutional with fully connected networks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Does not compare batch sizes; Figure 5 uses batch size 100.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization measures.

Zero training error should not be generalized to every training-set size.
